 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The New York Giants will return home to MetLife Stadium on Thursday night to face the Washington Commanders , looking to pick up their second straight win against an NFC East opponent.
 The Giants are coming off an ugly victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, improving their record to 5-2-1. The Commanders, meanwhile, lost a tight game to the Los Angeles Rams and dropped to 2-5-1.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement On Monday, the Giants opened as 1.5-point home favorites for the Thursday night matchup. This will be the second and final meeting between the two teams this season.
 With the NFC East rivals set to face off, here are three causes for concern for the Giants.
 Giants run struggles
 The Giants struggled to establish anything on the ground against Philadelphia, where their offensive line was dominated. Thursday's matchup figures to present an even tougher test. The Commanders have been significantly better against the run this season than the Eagles. Washington enters Week 10 ranked 12th in the NFL in opponent yards per game. Cam Skattebo should be a "full go" on Thursday. However, if the offensive line does not improve, it may be tough sledding for the Giants on the ground.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Quarterback J.J. McCarthy was brought in in part to add a dimension to the running game himself. After he was injured on one of his few designed quarterback runs in his two starts, the Giants may look to limit his exposure there. The offensive line will simply need to play better on Thursday.
 Susceptible to sacks
 The Giants also struggled against the pass rush on Sunday against the Eagles, who recorded six sacks and 14 tackles for loss. While the Giants defense delivered a stout performance, the protection issues up front remain a concern. With McCarthy already having been injured last week, the Giants will need to protect him better against sacks and give him more time to throw.
 Jayden Daniels
 In the teams' first meeting, Jayden Daniels was a problem for the Giants' defense. He rushed for 103 yards to lead the Commanders in rushing and scored two touchdowns on 26- and 38-yard runs. The Giants' run defense will need to make adjustments to better contain Daniels on Thursday night. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson may elect to keep a spy on the Washington quarterback.
